entries.claim: With one design, a rejected name throws away the user's dump. The "Doesn't fit, or is taken" retry (line 205) ends on the name line alone, but the brief route only carries the dump forward after the documents question, or after the name line alone when a which-design exchange came in between. With one design no which-design exchange ever happens, so a later `/seldon brief` falls to "Otherwise, reopen it" and asks what should change.
entries.failure_scenario: Seed only `.planning/seldon/brief.md` (one design). The user runs `/seldon <new dump text>` and Seldon shows the name line and the documents question. The user replies `My App`, which doesn't fit, so Seldon writes nothing and ends on the name line alone (lines 205-206). The user then types `/seldon brief`. The brief route (lines 107-113) checks: the last turn did not end on the documents question, and no which-design exchange happened. That leaves "Otherwise, reopen it": Seldon reads brief.md and asks what should change, and the dump is never applied. The user has to type it again, which is the outcome phase 3 D-02 and the plan's Task 3 bullet say must not happen. The retry also removed the documents question, so "Documents question answered" can no longer take the user to rerun the brief or go on from it.

entries.claim: The `<rules>` bullet still says each check runs "exactly as written there", and "The check" still says to run "exactly this" with `.planning/seldon`. The new paragraph at lines 259-264 says that with a named design a check runs on `.planning/seldon/<name>`. The diff updated the first `<rules>` bullet to point to the working folder but left this commands bullet unchanged, so the rules and §2 now say different things.
entries.failure_scenario: A named design `.planning/seldon/foo/` is being written while a top-level design also exists. A model that follows the `<rules>` bullet literally runs `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/check.mjs --brief .planning/seldon`. check.mjs accepts any directory (main(), lines 256-266), so it checks the top-level brief.md and prints its "conforms" line. The named design's brief is never checked, yet the step ends by repeating that passing line and asking the user to confirm it.

counter_evidence.note: Every .planning/seldon/ file path in this skill, fixed lines and check commands included, names that file in the working folder, and a check on a named design runs on .planning/seldon/<name>. The rules bullet at line 42 says to run each check exactly as written in its check section, and this paragraph defines what that section path names, so the two agree.
